clue.text: A story about Eugene in America

indicators.note: about means the story's word goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a story is a lie, a tall tale
Eugene Aram was a notorious 18th-century English murderer, subject of a famous poem by Thomas Hood

explanation.surface: Someone tells a tale about a man called Eugene who lived in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eugene' is a crossword favourite for ARAM, from the murderer Eugene Aram; the definition is cryptically loose, naming a place found in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Laramie is a city in Wyoming, so it is a place to be found within the United States.

clue.text: The French island state is secular

parts.note: la is French for the
Cal is an abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A French island territory has no established church.
explanation.definitionFit: Laical means relating to laypeople rather than clergy, hence not religious.

clue.text: Rake around, boy, for food

indicators.note: around means the rake's word wraps round the boy

parts.note: a rake is a roue, a dissolute man
a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A garden tool is moved around by a boy looking for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a garden tool but is a libertine.
explanation.definitionFit: A roulade is a rolled dish, such as a rolled meat or sponge.

clue.text: Shop girl in motorway eating area

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, read as MI
a dinette is a small dining space

explanation.surface: A shop assistant is found at a motorway service restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A midinette is a Parisian shop assistant or seamstress.

clue.text: Record awards announced for businesses

parts.note: to record data is to enter it

indicators.note: announced means the word for awards is heard spoken rather than seen

parts.note: awards are prizes

explanation.surface: A list of prizewinners is read out for companies.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprises are companies or commercial ventures.

clue.text: Myth about Queen Victoria, for instance, is easily demolished

indicators.note: about means the myth's word wraps round the royal letters

parts.note: a myth is a fable
RI, Regina Imperatrix, queen and empress, as Victoria was

explanation.surface: A legend surrounding Queen Victoria crumbles at the slightest push.
explanation.definitionFit: Friable describes something crumbly that breaks apart easily.

clue.text: Starts to flaunt abbreviated dress in short-lived fashion

indicators.note: Starts to points at the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Showing off a short dress is a passing trend.
explanation.definitionFit: A fad is a craze that quickly passes.

clue.text: Conclude part of town is in ferment

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters within the following words

explanation.surface: A district of the town is in uproar, someone deduces.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce from evidence.

clue.text: It's wrong about Sandhurst one has a female servant

indicators.note: about means the word for wrong encloses the other letters

parts.note: wrong means bad
Sandhurst is the Royal Military Academy, RMA, the British army officer school
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: It is scandalous that a Sandhurst officer keeps a maid.
explanation.definitionFit: A barmaid is a woman who serves drinks in a pub.

clue.text: Oriental depression — consumed by sloth

parts.note: E for east, the oriental direction
a dent is a depression
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: An Eastern despondency has been swallowed up by idleness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the sin of laziness but is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloths belong to the toothless mammal group, along with anteaters and armadillos.

clue.text: One sister had an escort but was drowned

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a sister in religion is a nun
to have an escort is to have dated someone

explanation.surface: A nun went out on a date and ended up in deep water.
explanation.definitionFit: Inundated means flooded or swamped by water, close to submerged.

clue.text: Falsify form

explanation.definitionFit: To falsify a document is to counterfeit it; to form metal is to shape it at an anvil.

clue.text: No artist falls back a second time

indicators.note: back means the remaining letters are read from right to left
No means the artist is absent from the waterfall's name

parts.note: Niagara is the famous falls
RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter who has given up stumbles over once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing RA from NIAGARA leaves NIAGA, which turned backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means once more, repeated a further occasion.

clue.text: Scarlet could be right beast to Robin!

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the colour scarlet suits a creature well, addressing Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: R plus BEAST shuffles to BREAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbreast is a traditional name for the robin, from its orange-red chest.

clue.text: Notes a receiver collected without being exposed

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
a fence receives stolen goods
without means less

explanation.surface: A recipient gathered messages without being seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' suggests a telephone; it is a dealer in stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open to attack is having no protection.

clue.text: It enables one to get money from a reputable landlord

definitions.text: It enables one to get money

parts.note: a landlord lets property, so is a letter
someone reputable is of credit, trustworthy

explanation.surface: A trustworthy landlord helps you obtain cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' must be read as one who lets, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank document authorising payment to the holder, letting a traveller draw funds abroad.

clue.text: Check school during break

indicators.note: during means the school word sits inside the break

parts.note: a break is a rest
to school is to train

explanation.surface: Pupils are told to behave at break time.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint holds back or curbs, as a check does.

clue.text: A shopkeeper the farmhouse victims needed?

explanation.definitionFit: A seller of goods; also one who puts tails back, as the nursery-rhyme mice wanted after the farmer's wife cut theirs off.

clue.text: Say one's piece when person feels sex has changed

indicators.note: has changed signals the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark about a person whose gender identity has altered.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak your mind is to voice what you think.

clue.text: Upholstery in the station lacking style

indicators.note: lacking means the style word is dropped from the station

parts.note: Paddington is a London railway terminus
ton means fashionable style

explanation.surface: Furniture in a railway station looks unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Padding is the stuffing material inside furniture.

clue.text: Beat girl in the London walk

parts.note: to lam is to beat
Beth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is beaten during a stroll around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lambeth Walk is a famous Cockney dance song, named after a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The district name completes the title of the 1930s Cockney dance.

clue.text: A man of the world

parts.note: not a sophisticate but any human living on earth, as opposed to a god

explanation.definitionFit: A mortal is a human being subject to death, an earthly creature.

clue.text: A don pushed into the river — he had it coming to him

definitions.text: he had it coming to him

indicators.note: pushed into means one piece is shoved inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
to don clothes is to dress

explanation.surface: An academic is shoved into a river, and he deserved it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher but is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: The recipient of a letter is the one it was sent to.

clue.text: The records are on order, of course

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
the OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: The discs are ordered, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like 'naturally'; course alone is the definition, a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is an English racecourse, home of the Derby.

clue.text: Lover finds me wearing a jumper

indicators.note: wearing means the jumper goes round the other piece like a garment

parts.note: a kangaroo, or roo, is a jumper

explanation.surface: A sweetheart discovers me in a knitted sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater, as the British call it, but is the leaping kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Romeo is the archetypal ardent suitor.

clue.text: See outrageous sin in these joints

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold

indicators.note: outrageous suggests the letters are thrown into wild disorder

explanation.surface: Look at the shocking wickedness that goes on in these establishments.
explanation.definitionFit: Loins are cuts of meat, as joints are for roasting.

clue.text: American company head may live in quiet new square

indicators.note: in means the living piece sits inside the other letters

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music
a T-square, so T
to live somewhere is to reside

explanation.surface: An American boss might dwell in a peaceful, newly built square.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage the chief executive of a corporation is often given this title.

clue.text: Criticize god

explanation.definitionFit: To slate a play is to give it a bad review; the Greek deity of shepherds is a god.

clue.text: I'm green adopting this diet

indicators.note: adopting suggests the letters take up a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dieter declares they are going green with a new eating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of food and exercise.

clue.text: Latches broken in bookcase?

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: The catches on a bookcase have snapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookcase' suggests furniture; read it as a case for carrying books.
explanation.definitionFit: A school bag carries books, so it is a case for them.
